t: This is Westminster School, tucked into the precincts of Westminster Abbey. It descends from a charity school run by Benedictine monks before the Norman Conquest, and its existence is clear from the early fourteenth century. Elizabeth the First is named as its founder, and so is Pope Alexander the Third. The school motto, Dat Deus Incrementum, means God gave the growth. Among its people, the art historian and broadcaster Andrew Graham-Dixon was born here, and the aviator C. W. A. Scott, who won the 1934 air race from London to Melbourne, died here.
